- [X] MI325X DSpark only: still ASM
- [X] MI325X DCP only (no drafter): still ASM
- [X] MI325X DSpark+DCP (this PR): target verify (qlen>1) + later qlen==1 decode

ons", "num_concurrent": 32, "max_retries": 10, "max_gen_toks": 2048, "tokenizer_backend":"None","tokenized_requests":"False" }' --tasks gsm8k --b

commits.pr_title: [Quantization] Support packed NVFP4 Qwen4Exp PLE embeddings
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Enable the `local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4` checkpoint to run on **1x DGX Spark without CPU or disk PLE offloading**. Its packed NVFP4 ngram table occupies 26.822 GiB and remains resident in CUDA memory. The PR's resident path was validated on one GB10 with a 4,096-token context, 2 GiB KV cache, and MTP disabled; model loading reported 97.47 GiB.

Fixes #56272.

Support `ple_embedding_dtype="nvfp4"` in Qwen4Exp ngram embeddings. The [local-inference-lab checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4/tree/ada4da32a583a78aa47299f45a70603c950490b8) stores each logical 160-value row as 80 packed E2M1 bytes and 10 E4M3 block scales, with one FP32 global scale. Upstream currently selects an unquantized table for this explicit storage format inside a ModelOpt mixed-precision checkpoint.

The change adds an embedding method to the existing device/pinned-host storage interface. Both paths keep packed weights and block scales in their original storage and decode only the requested rows. Lookup reuses the existing E2M1 decoder and produces activation-dtype rows before ETP reduction. The loader copies each checkpoint shard's overlap with the local ETP vocabulary range and validates coverage after all weight streams finish, along with the global scale, tensor shapes, and storage dtypes.

Related work was checked on September 10, 2026. [#54882](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54882) and [#55334](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55334) concern an FP8 PLE table inside a model with NVFP4 body weights. [#53899](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53899) contains an older NVFP4 PLE implementation within offload work, but its mixed-precision dispatch does not select this checkpoint's explicit NVFP4 table. [#42791](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42791) adds generic quantized vocabulary embeddings. This change targets the serialized split PLE layout through the storage interface merged in [#54371](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54371).

AI assistance was used to develop and test this change.

## Test Plan

Extend the existing PLE suite with streamed packed-weight/block-scale loading across ETP boundaries, missing row coverage, malformed storage/global scales, independent numerical decoding, compiled GPU lookup, CUDA graph replay with changing IDs, empty/padded inputs, and pinned-host prefetch. Add the NVFP4 cases to the existing H200 Qwen4Exp CI lane.

Test base: `b28c3e1568bfae930f61d4b24940e47528c85d4a`, with the matching upstream precompiled CUDA wheel, Torch `2.13.0+cu130`, and FlashInfer `0.6.18.post1`. GPUs: one isolated RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q and one DGX Spark / GB10. The Spark run used the published PR commit `e251861aab69d3eb438d1a76ddec036ae45cfd4c`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v --tb=short --timeout=300 \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_config.py
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -v --tb=short --timeout=600 \
  tests/compile/h100/test_startup.py::test_moe_startup
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run --files \
  vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py .buildkite/test_areas/models_basic.yaml
.venv/bin/python -m pre_commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/models/qwen4_exp/nvidia/ngram_embedding.py \
  tests/models/qwen4_exp/test_ple.py
```

Full-model text-generation validation used the pinned checkpoint above (image/video inputs disabled), a 4,096-token context, 512-token prefill chunks, four sequences, 2 GiB of KV cache, and full/piecewise CUDA graph capture sizes `[1, 2, 4]`. The offline harness ran with `PYTHONPATH=/opt/ngram/vllm:/run/ngram /opt/ngram/.venv/bin/python /run/ngram/model_smoke.py` on Max-Q and `model_smoke_spark.py` on Spark. Spark used `engram_config={"cpu_offload":false}` and `cpu_offload_gb=0`; Max-Q used pinned-host PLE storage. It checked selected rows from the complete table against an independent decoder, then four chat prompts and the first 32 canonical GSM8K test examples (temperature 0, thinking disabled, 768 output tokens).

## Test Result

- PLE and configuration suites: 76 passed on Max-Q and 76 passed on DGX Spark.
- Compilation startup canary on Max-Q: 2 passed.
- Actual checkpoint sample: 8 rows of width 160 matched an independent E2M1/FP8/global-scale reference exactly after BF16 conversion, through both device lookup and pinned-host prefetch with simulated ETP ownership.
- CPU PLE/configuration suites: 43 passed, 33 skipped because CUDA was unavailable.
- Pre-commit, including Python 3.10 type checks, and manual Python 3.12 type checks: passed.
- Full checkpoint loaded with 26.822 GiB of packed PLE weights/scales in CUDA memory on Spark and pinned host memory on Max-Q. On both devices, selected rows from the full table, including addresses beyond 32-bit offsets, matched the independent BF16 reference exactly.
- Full-model startup captured all six CUDA graphs on each device. All four generation checks passed on each, including a prompt requiring chunked prefill.
- GSM8K smoke evaluation: 31/32 exact numeric answers (96.875%) on each GPU. On each device, the remaining response hit the 768-token limit. This is a small smoke evaluation, not a full benchmark or comparison with the checkpoint publisher's runtime.

The checkpoint uses preview architecture names. Validation normalizes them with `hf_overrides={"model_type":"qwen4_exp","architectures":["Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration"]}`. PLE offload is disabled on Spark and enabled on Max-Q. It selects `kernel_config={"linear_backend":"marlin"}` because the automatic MXFP8 linear backend rejects the checkpoint's 96-output GDN projection. Real multi-GPU collectives and MTP have not been validated with this PR.

## Single-Spark reference measurements

Separate end-to-end measurements on September 10, 2026 compared the [local-inference-lab checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/local-inference-lab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4/tree/ada4da32a583a78aa47299f45a70603c950490b8) using its b12x runtime with the [NVIDIA checkpoint](https://huggingface.co/nvidia/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-NVFP4/tree/fc694b54fb0174e0913e6adf86691ef85a4ead47) using upstream vLLM plus disk PLE offload patches. These measurements provide context for fitting the checkpoints on one DGX Spark. They were collected independently of this PR and do not measure its performance impact.

Workload: 32,768 shared prefix tokens, 2,048 suffix tokens, and 256 output tokens; streaming chat, temperature 0, three warmups per cell, and concurrency 1/4/8 with 10/40/80 measured requests. Both runtimes used one GB10, TP1/PP1, a 40,960-token context limit, prefix caching, chunked prefill, and MTP with four draft tokens. Latency and TTFT are means; decode throughput is aggregate active decode throughput from AIPerf.

| Checkpoint / runtime | Concurrency | Requests | Latency (s) | TTFT (s) | Decode (tok/s) | Acceptance length |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| local-inference-lab / b12x | 1 | 10 | 11.27 | 3.40 | 32.41 | 2.40 |
| local-inference-lab / b12x | 4 | 40 | 28.19 | 5.44 | 36.31 | 2.13 |
| local-inference-lab / b12x | 8 | 80 | 45.99 | 6.75 | 43.44 | 2.20 |
| NVIDIA / vLLM with disk PLE | 1 | 10 | 14.30 | 3.45 | 23.51 | 2.64 |
| NVIDIA / vLLM with disk PLE | 4 | 40 | 29.60 | 5.09 | 34.25 | 2.39 |
| NVIDIA / vLLM with disk PLE | 8 | 80 | 44.34 | 7.12 | 45.92 | 2.59 |

Each checkpoint completed all 130 measured requests with zero errors and zero preemptions. Every measured response contained 256 output tokens. Acceptance length is `1 + accepted_tokens / draft_steps`, calculated from server counters.

The local checkpoint's packed PLE payload is 26.822 GiB, held in b12x's resident managed CUDA weight storage with no explicit CPU or disk PLE offload; KV cache was 8 GiB FP8. The NVIDIA checkpoint's FP8 PLE payload is 47.684 GiB, served through disk-backed mmap and the OS page cache; KV cache was 10 GiB BF16. Quantization, backends, and prefix reuse also differ (27,216 versus 30,704 reused tokens per request), so this is a comparison of complete configurations. Each cell is a single run, and accuracy equivalence was not evaluated. Host swap activity was observed, so no swap-free claim is made.

<details>
<summary>Reference runtime revisions</summary>

- Local runtime: [vLLM `aba94d396`](https://github.com/local-inference-lab/vllm/tree/aba94d396d27ea92a2044ad024c003b36da505d3), [b12x `75ffee637`](https://github.com/lukealonso/b12x/tree/75ffee6375b0577ce2c8d6931ffacefda3ecbdd6).
- NVIDIA runtime: upstream [`73029d424`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/tree/73029d42441321b631779db3475031f5ec26dd6c), with [#54129 at `50a061f79`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/50a061f792f36364f5f95a93eee21f1e9d77f65e), [#54882 at `d4d703caf`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/d4d703caf908786416585ceb1f369e2e0363358b), [#55513 at `60ad959b6`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/60ad959b6f1a5c8f602edbd608c8decbc0788c50), and [#56026 at `4a365dee4`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/4a365dee4aed8ae3135213b4cf6ce04f6d82e756).
- AIPerf [`00ba1c5db`](https://github.com/ai-dynamo/aiperf/tree/00ba1c5db3fbe5f7e9852fcba2f1f0e269d0f13a); Torch `2.13.0+cu130`, FlashInfer `0.6.18`, NVIDIA driver `580.95.05`.

</details>

commits.pr_title: [MRV2] Keep warmup out of the EPLB load stats
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

MRV2 warmup forwards record expert load into `expert_load_pass` like real ones. The router kernel records during the forward, so skipping or suppressing the EPLB step afterwards does not keep that load out of the stats. It lands in the next real step. This happens at startup and on every elastic EP re-warm right after the rebalance.

This adds `EPLBController.suppress()` which turns off both the EPLB step and `should_record_tensor` and puts both back when done. It is used for `skip_eplb=True` in `step_eplb_after`, around MRV2 `compile_or_warm_up_model` and around `profile_cudagraph_memory`. `EplbState.step` now also zeroes the dummy load before the profile early return.

MRV1 has the same recording issue on a serving rank. #57151 fixes it there.

Split out of #53934

## Test Plan

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_model_runner_v2_cudagraph_profiling.py
```

## Test Result

12 passed and 1 skipped. ruff and mypy pass. Not run on GPUs.

CC @itayalroy

commits.pr_title: [Feat] Add text-only OpenAI Decisions API
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Adds a text-only `/v1/decisions` endpoint following the [OpenAI API format](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/decisions).

Builds on #59299 and #60677, now merged into `main`.

## Claims

Supports predicate, choice, and score questions using shared label reads under `vllm/entrypoints/openai/decisions`. `/v1/decisions` is available by default on supported generation models and returns 501 when no generation read strategy is available. `/v1/systemone` also supports Clef-Omni pooling models from #61064. The new endpoint accepts text strings or user messages and returns ordered answers with probabilities and token usage.

## Validation

- 137 CPU tests passed on the rebased commit, including Clef-Flash, Liquid d1, and Clef-Omni strategy coverage, DiffusionGemma, launcher routing, cache-salt/tracing behavior, HTTP error handling, logging, limits, Qwen tokenization, and shared generative scoring. All-files pre-commit with the CI manual stage passed.
- Local SDK/schema checks passed without model inference. The OpenAPI schema test collects after extending the existing SmolVLM 501 handling to `/v1/decisions`; its live GPU case runs in Buildkite.
- Qwen3-0.6B GPU end-to-end tests on a DGX Spark: all 15 endpoint tests passed without an endpoint flag before this rebase and the test relocation. The run used `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.35` to share the device. The current checkout could not rerun GPU tests because its NVIDIA driver is unavailable.
- A small balanced Qwen3-0.6B factual eval through `/v1/decisions` scored 8/16: 6/12 predicates and 2/4 choices. All six true predicates received probabilities below 0.5. Direct Chat Completions with the same predicate prompt also returned `false` for a true case, so this result needs a stronger-model follow-up. Live OpenAI comparison remains pending.

```bash
HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \

  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_decisions.py \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_question_types.py \
  tests/entrypoints/scale_out/test_factories.py \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/generative_scoring/test_generative_scoring.py -q
# 137 passed

  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_openai_schema.py --collect-only -q
# 1 test collected; GPU server unavailable locally

UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/uv-cache .venv/bin/pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual

.venv/bin/python -m pytest --noconftest -o addopts='' \
  -o cache_dir=/tmp/decisions-pytest-cache \
  tests/entrypoints/generate/structured_decisions/test_structured_decisions_e2e.py -q
# 15 passed with Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B, before the test relocation

.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/decisions/test_decisions_e2e.py --collect-only -q
# 2 tests collected in the current location; GPU server unavailable locally
```

The CPU HTTP tests use a test engine and a cached Qwen tokenizer. The worktree used existing precompiled CUDA extensions for model registry inspection; this PR changes no C/CUDA code. The earlier GPU run used a temporary copy of this PR's Python source with `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.35`. The 16-case factual eval was a temporary script with six true and six false predicates and balanced choice positions, also before this rebase.

</details>

## Details

For this MVP: no images or refusal scoring, and at most 64 questions and 26 choices. Confidence is not calibrated to OpenAI's models.

Duplicate checks found no other open PR for this endpoint. #59299 added the shared backend and #60677 ungated `/v1/systemone`; this PR moves shared modules under `openai/decisions` and adds the OpenAI-format endpoint. Built with Codex assistance.

``` python

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Concurrent traffic driver to force adaptive draft-budget trimming."""
import json
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from concurrent.futures import ThreadPoolExecutor

PORT = sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv) > 1 else "8002"
N = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 16
MAXTOK = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 8

URL = f"http://localhost:{PORT}/v1/completions"
PROMPTS = [
    "Explain the theory of relativity in simple terms.",
    "Write a poem about a rainy day in the city.",
    "Summarize the history of the Roman Empire.",
    "Describe how a neural network learns.",
    "List five facts about the human brain.",
    "Tell a short story about a lost dog.",
    "Explain photosynthesis to a child.",
    "What are the causes of climate change?",
    "Describe the water cycle step by step.",
    "Write about the importance of sleep.",
    "Explain how the internet works.",
    "Give a recipe for chocolate chip cookies.",
    "Describe the life cycle of a butterfly.",
    "Explain the stock market in simple words.",
    "Write about the benefits of exercise.",
    "Describe the process of making coffee.",
]


def one(i):
    body = json.dumps({
        "model": "deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash",
        "prompt": PROMPTS[i % len(PROMPTS)],
        "max_tokens": MAXTOK,
        "temperature": 0.7,
        "seed": i,
    }).encode()
    req = urllib.request.Request(URL, data=body, headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
    t0 = time.time()
    try:
        with urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=1800) as r:
            d = json.load(r)
        return i, d.get("usage", {}).get("completion_tokens"), time.time() - t0
    except Exception as e:
        return i, f"ERR {type(e).__name__}: {e}", time.time() - t0


with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=N) as ex:
    for i, ntok, dt in ex.map(one, range(N)):
        print(f"req {i}: tokens={ntok} in {dt:.1f}s", flush=True)
print("DONE")
```

```bash
for r in $(seq 1 40); do
  .venv/bin/python repro_60945_e2e/drive.py 8011 1024 16 > /tmp/pr59166/run_$r.log 2>&1
  ok=$(grep -cE "^req .*tokens=" /tmp/pr59166/run_$r.log)
  err=$(grep -cE "ERR" /tmp/pr59166/run_$r.log)
  printf "round %s: completed=%s err=%s\n" "$r" "$ok" "$err"
  if grep -qE "illegal memory access|EngineCore failed|CUDA error|Traceback" "$SERVE_LOG"; then
    echo "!!! CRASH at round $r"; crash=1; break
  fi
done
echo "crash=$crash"
curl -s http://localhost:8011/health -w "health %{http_code}\n" -o /dev/null
```

commits.pr_title: [Attention] Set ALWAYS cudagraph support for FA4
commits.pr_body:
# Summary
This PR enables `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` cudagraph support for Flash Attention 4. The primary motivation is to enable adaptive verification (AV) with MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 + DFlash using the default attention backend (`FLASH_ATTN_DIFFKV`) on GB200.

`AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` means a FULL cudagraph captured for one batch layout can be replayed for any other layout with the same token count, including mixed prefill+decode batches and variable per-request query lengths. That holds for FA4 for three reasons:

1. No host-side scheduling state. Unlike FA3, FA4 builds no AOT scheduler metadata (aot_schedule is gated on fa_version == 3). All per-batch tiling is derived on device from cu_seqlens_q/seqused_k inside the captured kernels, so replays with a different layout recompute it correctly.
2. The grid does not depend on per-request lengths. The varlen tile scheduler sizes its grid from total_q (the padded token count, fixed per graph) and the batch size, not from max_seqlen_q.
3. Host-side specializations are conservative under an upper bound. FA4 does specialize on the host max_seqlen_q: it selects q_stage and, when max_seqlen_q * qhead_per_kvhead <= q_stage * tile_m, a static persistent scheduler that assumes at most one M-block per request. These are correct for any replay whose real query lengths do not exceed the captured max_seqlen_q. The runners guarantee that: mixed FULL graphs are captured with max_query_len = num_tokens, the worst case for the token count (MRV2 prepare_inputs_to_capture, V1 _dummy_run); decode and varlen-decode graphs are captured with the decode width and only replay batches within it; and dispatch matches a graph only when its max_query_len covers the batch.

FA2 still needs `AttentionCGSupport.UNIFORM_BATCH` because of its packed-GQA special case for max_query_len == 1 captures.

# Test Plan
- Kernel-level graph-replay checks, FA4 on GB200, MiMo-V2.5-Pro TP4 attention geometry (32/2 heads, head dims 192/128, SWA 128 with sinks, page sizes 16/64):
  - Varlen-decode replay (42 configs) and mixed prefill+decode full-graph replay (18 configs) both match eager bit-for-bit, including captures with tiny max_seqlen_k.
  - A negative control that captures with max_seqlen_q below the replayed lengths fails (max abs error 2.05), so the checks detect a broken replay.
- Without AV: Qwen3-8B gsm8k with FLASH_ATTN + cudagraph_mode=FULL, main vs PR: 88.48% vs 88.55%, within noise.
- With AV: MiMo-V2.5-Pro-FP4 + DFlash gsm8k (full 1319 questions), AV off vs on: 95.83% vs 96.29%, within noise. It also starts and serves coherent output with no attention overrides.

commits.pr_title: [CI] Shard quantization, pooling, multimodal APIs, core kernels and PCP eval automatically
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Enroll five NVIDIA CI steps in automatic runtime sharding, selecting long jobs from the [duration ranking](https://vllm-ci-dashboard.vercel.app/jobs) over the preceding 12 hours. Batch 5 of five independently based changes.

## Claims

Preserve the test commands and discovery scope while assigning tests using main timing data. Existing AMD fixed shards retain their effective commands and parallelism. Actual wall-time and cost improvements await Buildkite validation.

| Step | 12h median job min | Planned shards | Estimated test min/shard |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `quantization` | 22.5 | 4 | 15.6, 15.2, 15.2, 15.2 |
| `language-models-test-extended-pooling` | 22.4 | 5 | 16.4, 16.4, 16.4, 16.5, 16.8 |
| `entrypoints-integration-multimodal` | 22.2 | 2 | 10.7, 10.8 |
| `kernels-core-operation-test` | 20.7 | 4 | 13.6, 13.6, 13.6, 13.6 |
| `lm-eval-pcp-4xb200` | 20.6 | 2 | 13.1, 7.2 |


## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files <changed YAML files>`: passed.
- `pytest buildkite/tests/pipeline_generator/test_runtime_shard.py -q` in ci-infra: 24 passed.
- `runtime_shard.plan_step` previews: all five steps produce multiple shards.

commits.pr_title: [Mooncake] Allow Mamba cache mode `none` for capacity-only workers
commits.pr_body:
Allow Mooncake capacity-only consumers to use Mamba cache mode `none`, which is selected when prefix caching is disabled.

Disabling prefix caching is required for Kimi K3 TP8 + DEP16 disaggregated serving because heterogeneous physical blocks per logical KV block are not supported with prefix caching for Mamba hybrid models. Otherwise, this configuration triggers the [runtime error](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/d766ac98285bf1a84acfeb37c99c73d5396d4df6/vllm/distributed/kv_transfer/kv_connector/v1/nixl/base_worker.py#L2542):
```
        if (
            self._has_mamba
            and remote_physical_per_logical
            != self._physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block
            and self.vllm_config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching
        ):
            raise RuntimeError(
                "Prefix caching with heterogeneous physical_blocks_per_logical "
                "is not supported for Mamba hybrid models. "
                f"Local: {self._physical_blocks_per_logical_kv_block}, "
                f"Remote: {remote_physical_per_logical}. "
                "Disable prefix caching with --no-enable-prefix-caching."
            )
```

commits.pr_title: Fix write-after-write hazard in xpu KV RoPE triton kernel
commits.pr_body:
The KV branch of `_xpu_qnorm_rope_kernel` copied all HEAD_DIM elements into the output, then overwrote the RoPE region with the rotated values. These stores target overlapping addresses with no ordering guarantee, so on XPU the RoPE positions were non-deterministic run-to-run, making greedy decode unstable.

Mask the full copy to the NoPE region so the RoPE region is written only by the rotated stores, matching the Q branch.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][MoE] Clamp BLOCK_SIZE_K to the FP8 quantization block in the batched Triton MoE
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

`invoke_moe_batched_triton_kernel` (the `BATCHED_TRITON` FP8 MoE used with DeepEP low-latency and other batched-activation all2all backends when DeepGEMM is unavailable or disabled) takes `BLOCK_SIZE_K` straight from the tuned config. With block-quantized FP8 weights the kernel loads one weight and activation scale per `BLOCK_K` tile (`offs_ks = k * BLOCK_K // group_k`), so a `BLOCK_SIZE_K` wider than the 128-wide quantization block applies one block's scale to the next block's values. 53 of the 64 shipped `fp8_w8a8, block_shape=[128,128]` configs pick `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256 for some batch sizes. The standard path already clamps (`fused_moe.py:843-844`); this PR applies the same clamp in the batched launcher.

No existing issue or PR covers this (searched `fused_batched_moe BLOCK_SIZE_K`, `BLOCK_SIZE_K batched fp8`, `batched triton block_shape BLOCK_K`). Rechecked 2026-10-08: open PR #51605 resizes batched Triton MoE tiles on XPU and edits the same launcher, but it does not clamp `BLOCK_SIZE_K` for block-quantized FP8 on CUDA; whichever lands second needs a small rebase.

## Claims

- Fixes wrong outputs from the batched Triton FP8 block-quant MoE whenever the selected config has `BLOCK_SIZE_K` > the quantization block. GLM-5.3 FP8 with DeepEP low-latency and DeepGEMM off: GSM8K 0.02 → 0.93.
- No change when the config already has `BLOCK_SIZE_K` <= 128, for per-token / per-tensor FP8, or for unquantized dtypes (`block_shape is None`).
- A smaller `BLOCK_K` can cost some kernel speed for the affected configs; correctness requires it, and the standard Triton MoE path made the same choice.

## Validation

**Unit test**: `test_batched_mm` (`tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py`) only ever ran FP8 with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 32, below the quantization block, so it could not catch this. It now also runs FP8 with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256.

| Build | `test_batched_mm` |
|---|---|
| this branch | 168 passed (216 skipped: non-FP8 dtypes and invalid quantization combinations) |
| without the fix | 12 failed: every FP8 block-quant case with `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256 and K = 1024 (K = 128 is a single block, so it cannot show the bug) |

Whole `test_batched_moe.py` with the fix (H200): 470 passed, 0 failed. These counts were re-run on the branch after rebasing onto main @ 240785b8 (the rebase did not change the patch); the GSM8K runs below predate the rebase. pre-commit passes.

**End to end, GLM-5.3 FP8** (1 x 8 H200, DP4 x TP2, EP8, `--all2all-backend deepep_low_latency`, `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0`, which selects the `BATCHED_TRITON` FP8 MoE backend; fp8 KV; `lm_eval` GSM8K 5-shot):

| Build | CUDA graphs | Questions | GSM8K flexible / strict |
|---|---|---|---|
| main | `NONE` | 200 | 0.020 / 0.005 |
| main + this fix | `NONE` | 200 | 0.930 / 0.930 |
| main | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | 1,319 | 0.012 / 0.005 |
| main + this fix | `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` | 1,319 | 0.923 / 0.923 |
| reference: main, DeepEP high-throughput (`FLASHINFER_CUTLASS` MoE) | `NONE` | 1,319 | 0.927 / 0.928 |

The two `main + this fix` rows ran with `VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0` (V1 model runner); the other rows used the default V2 model runner. The unit tests and GSM8K runs above were built on main at 4a705c7b5; `fused_batched_moe.py`, `test_batched_moe.py` and the test helpers it imports are unchanged from there to this PR's base.

**In production (vLLM 0.29.0)**: GLM-5.3 RL decode on DeepEP low-latency with DP32/EP32 used `E=8,N=2048,device_name=NVIDIA_H200,dtype=fp8_w8a8,block_shape=[128,128].json`, which picks `BLOCK_SIZE_K` = 256 at M = 3072. Trainer-vs-inference mismatch KL was 0.139 / 0.149 instead of the usual 0.017 until we capped `BLOCK_SIZE_K` at 128 in a copy of that config (`VLLM_TUNED_CONFIG_FOLDER`).

<details>
<summary>Reproduction commands</summary>

```bash
# unit test
pytest -v tests/kernels/moe/test_batched_moe.py::test_batched_mm

# GSM8K
VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 VLLM_MOE_USE_DEEP_GEMM=0 vllm serve zai-org/GLM-5.3 --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --data-parallel-size 4 --enable-expert-parallel --all2all-backend deepep_low_latency \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 8192
lm_eval --model local-completions \
  --model_args model=zai-org/GLM-5.3,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=256,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5
```
</details>

## Details

**Root cause:** `moe_mmk` iterates K in `BLOCK_K` steps and, for block quantization (`group_k > 0 and group_n > 0`), loads the scales for `k_start // group_k` once per step (`fused_batched_moe.py:162-170`). The launcher passes `config["BLOCK_SIZE_K"]` through unchanged (`:452`). With `BLOCK_K` = 256 and `group_k` = 128, the second half of every K tile is scaled with the first half's scales. `fused_experts_impl` avoids this: its launcher `invoke_fused_moe_triton_kernel` clamps `BLOCK_SIZE_K` to `min(block_shape)` before launch (`fused_moe.py:843-844`), but `BatchedTritonExperts`, which reads the same tuned config files through `try_get_optimal_moe_config` (`fused_batched_moe.py:934`), does not.

**How it was found:** GLM-5.3 RL with prefill/decode disaggregation; the decode instance (DeepEP low-latency, DeepGEMM off) produced much higher trainer-vs-inference KL than the prefill instance. The layer-level GEMM output matched the reference only after capping `BLOCK_SIZE_K`.

**Fix:** clamp `BLOCK_K` exactly as the standard path does.

**AI assistance:** Claude Code was used to trace the root cause, write the patch and test, run the validations above, and draft this description. I reviewed every changed line, can explain and defend the change, and checked the test results above.

commits.pr_title: [HiSparse] Read GPU-resident KV directly for mixed and BF16 prefills
commits.pr_body:
Fixes #60420.

**Problem on main:** with HiSparse, a prefill batched with any decode copies its entire KV history into a temporary GPU buffer on every layer of every chunk, then joins the decode and prefill outputs with `torch.cat`. This happens even when all of its KV is already on GPU, which is the common case in aggregated serving. FlashMLA BF16 does the copy on every prefill. Startup profiling sees neither allocation. Two results:
- **Crash:** a long prompt arriving while other requests decode kills EngineCore with CUDA OOM, and the running requests die with it.
- **Slowdown:** the per-layer copy grows with context. A 1M-token prefill on FlashMLA BF16 takes 3.3x longer than without HiSparse.

**Now:** when all KV is on GPU, decode and prefill rows run in one kernel against the GPU pages, with no copy and no `torch.cat`. Covers FlashInfer, FlashAttn, FlashInfer SM120 and FlashMLA BF16 sparse MLA.

**Evidence:** 1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers with dummy weights, 2 requests decoding, then one 1.04M-token prompt. Peak is the largest per-step peak above the step's starting allocation.

```bash
vllm serve <GLM-5.3-NVFP4> --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 4}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --gpu-memory-utilization 0.97 \
  --scheduler-reserve-full-isl \
  --kv-transfer-config '{"kv_connector":"HiSparseConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_connector_extra_config":{"host_pool_gib":24}}'
```

| Path | main | this PR | no HiSparse |
|---|---|---|---|
| FlashInfer fp8, util 0.97 | **OOM at 934K** in `torch.cat`; peak 6.30 GiB | 58.6 s; peak 4.91 GiB | 53.7 s; peak 4.91 GiB |
| FlashMLA BF16, util 0.95 | 184 s; peak 6.58 GiB | 56.0 s; peak 4.48 GiB | 55.2 s; peak 4.48 GiB |

With debug logging, no host-staging calls happen with this PR.

**Tests**
- `pytest tests/v1/attention/test_sparse_mla_backends.py` (B200): 509 passed. The resident-mixed routing cases in `test_sparse_mqa_hisparse_lanes` fail on main.
- GSM8K, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4 with HiSparse, 4×B200 (1319 questions, 5-shot, FlashInfer sparse MLA), two runs each: 0.896 / 0.914 vs main 0.914 / 0.909.
- After merging #55866 (shared HiSparse forward), the 4-layer repro at util 0.97 still OOMs on main (12b005eefa, in `torch.cat`) and completes with this PR.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][ROCm][Kimi-K3] Stage fused KDA decode weights after loading
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

The ROCm Kimi-K3 fused KDA decode read uninitialized memory as its conv1d and gated-norm weights whenever weight loaders were skipped, as with `--load-format dummy`. This intermittently produced NaN logprobs. Those copies are now built from the final parameters after loading.

## Claims

- `process_weights_after_loading` stages `decode_conv1d_weight` and `decode_norm_weight` from `conv1d.weight` and `o_norm.weight`, and the two side-effect weight loaders are removed.
- This fixes the intermittent HTTP 400 (`Out of range float values are not JSON compliant: nan`) in `test_prefix_cache.py` on MI355.

## Validation

MI355 (gfx950), `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1`. In `test_prefix_cache.py[offload-partial]`, NaN runs went from 5 of 21 to 0 of 20. The new `test_decode_weights_staged_after_loading` fails before (18432/18432 elements are NaN) and passes after. `models/kimi_k3` passes: 311 passed.

The perf runs used `riverclouds/Kimi-K3-8L-dummy` at TP1, 5 interleaved runs per column, each with a fresh server. Values are mean ± sd.

| `vllm bench serve` (4096 in / 256 out, conc 16) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Request throughput (req/s) | 7.687 ± 0.025 | 7.672 ± 0.009 |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 634.4 ± 6.5 | 633.5 ± 2.5 |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 5.434 ± 0.004 | 5.454 ± 0.017 |

No real-weight Kimi-K3 checkpoint was available for an accuracy run. With real weights, the buffers receive the same values the loaders wrote before.

## Details

The fp32 copies from #50654 are non-persistent `torch.empty` buffers that were written only inside the conv1d and o_norm weight loaders. `DummyModelLoader` skips both, so the fused decode used whatever the allocator returned: usually zeros, sometimes NaN. That poisoned the recurrent state from the first decode step. The post-load hook runs for every loader, including layerwise reload (the buffer storage is reused, so CUDA graphs stay valid). It skips weights that arrive already processed. The NVIDIA `KimiK3DeltaAttention` has the same latent issue and is left for a follow-up. #59245 reads these buffers and will need a rebase.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used to draft this change. Every line was reviewed by the submitter.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep GateLinear batch invariant under VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, MoE models whose gate uses `GateLinear`'s specialized router GEMM tiers are not batch invariant. I found this while validating models for #27433 on NVIDIA GB300: `zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air`, `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2` and `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` all fail the batch-invariance suite. This PR makes `GateLinear` use the batch-invariant linear path in that mode.

## Claims

- GLM-4.5-Air, MiniMax-M2 and ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B pass the full batch-invariance suite on GB300 (22/22 each). Without the fix they fail 12, 16 and 6 of the 22 tests.
- New regression test `tests/v1/determinism/test_gate_linear_batch_invariant.py` fails without the fix on both Blackwell and Ampere and passes with it.
- No change when `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is off.

## Validation

NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3), driver 580.167.08, CUDA toolkit 13.1, torch 2.13.0+cu130, vLLM `f590eb2448` (`gate_linear.py` is unchanged between that commit and this PR's base).

**Model level.** Each test id of `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` run in its own process:

```bash
VLLM_TEST_MODEL=<model> VLLM_TP_SIZE=<tp> VLLM_TEST_TP_SIZE=<tp> \
  pytest -p no:rerunfailures "tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py::<test id>"
```

| Model | GPUs (TP) | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `zai-org/GLM-4.5-Air` | 2 | 12 failed, 10 passed | 22 passed |
| `MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M2` | 2 | 16 failed, 6 passed | 22 passed |
| `baidu/ERNIE-4.5-21B-A3B-PT` | 1 | 6 failed, 16 passed | 22 passed |

What fails without the fix:

- All three: the 6 needle tests (`Nondeterministic outputs detected`, 2 to 5 of 5 trials).
- GLM-4.5-Air and MiniMax-M2: the 6 `bs1_vs_bsN` bitwise tests (`Batch invariance violated` in 30 to 32 of 32 prompts).
- MiniMax-M2 only: the 3 ragged chunked-prefill tests and the decode/prefill logprob test (49 mismatches).

GLM-4.5-Air also fails the needle test at TP=1 (4 of 5 trials), so this is not a tensor-parallel effect. MiniMax-M2 used `VLLM_GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION=0.9`. For MiniMax-M2 and ERNIE the before and after runs were on two identical GB300 nodes at the same commit, one unmodified and one with this change.

Models whose results do not change: `Qwen/Qwen3-235B-A22B` passes the suite without the fix (its gate does not use the specialized tiers). `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat` and `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3.1` pass the needle and bitwise tests with and without it.

**Unit level.** `pytest tests/v1/determinism/test_gate_linear_batch_invariant.py`:

| GPU | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| NVIDIA GB300 (SM 10.3) | 10 failed, 2 passed | 12 passed |
| NVIDIA A10 (SM 8.6) | 6 failed, 6 passed | 12 passed |

**No regression with the mode off.** `tests/kernels/test_ll_bf16_gemm.py` and `tests/kernels/test_gate_linear_rocm_dispatch.py` give 19 passed, 136 skipped both before and after (A10). `pre-commit` passes.

## Details

**Root cause.** `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` is where `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is honored for linear layers (it calls `linear_batch_invariant`). `GateLinear.forward` returns from tiers 1 to 4 before reaching it. Those tiers also dispatch on the number of tokens:

- tier 1 (`ll_bf16_gemm`) is used for `M <= 16`, otherwise the cuBLAS `out_dtype` tier;
- tier 2 (fp32 kernel) is used for `M <= 32`, otherwise BF16x3 or `F.linear`;
- tier 3 (BF16x3) picks its tile size and split-K from the token count in `_pick_tile_config`.

So the router logits of one row can come from a different kernel, or a different K-reduction order, depending on how many tokens share the batch. A small difference in the logits can change the selected experts, which then changes logprobs and tokens. GLM-4.5-Air and ERNIE-4.5 have fp32 gates that take the BF16x3 tier on Blackwell; MiniMax-M2's gate shape (3072 x 256) also has the fp32 kernel, so it switches kernels at `M = 32`.

To localize it I compared the same prompt alone and inside a mixed batch on GLM-4.5-Air. Disabling fused grouped top-k did not restore bitwise-equal logprobs; disabling the `GateLinear` tiers did.

These tiers were added between June and September (#46385, #42562, #47973, #55899), and #58234 moved all MoE models to `GateLinear`, after most of the batch-invariance model validation was done.

**Fix.** The tier eligibility flags are now false when `envs.VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT` is set, so `forward` falls through to tier 5 (`ReplicatedLinear`), which uses the batch-invariant matmul. The flags are also what `set_out_dtype` and the kernel warmup read, so warmup for the unused kernels is skipped too.

**Cost.** In batch-invariant mode the gate no longer uses the specialized kernels. Median time of one `GateLinear.forward` call on GB300 (bf16 input, 200 iterations after warmup):

| Gate (hidden x experts) | M | Specialized tiers | Batch-invariant path |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| fp32, 3072 x 256 | 1 | 54 us | 139 us |
| fp32, 3072 x 256 | 1024 | 134 us | 145 us |
| fp32, 4096 x 128 | 1 | 105 us | 146 us |
| fp32, 4096 x 128 | 1024 | 98 us | 155 us |
| bf16 with fp32 output, 7168 x 256 | 1 | 73 us | 131 us |
| bf16 with fp32 output, 7168 x 256 | 1024 | 72 us | 133 us |

That is 1.1x to 2.7x per call, between 10 and 90 microseconds, and only when the mode is on. I disabled all four tiers because that is the configuration I validated. If a tier can be shown to be batch invariant on its own, it could be re-enabled separately.

**CI.** The new test is added to the H100 and B200 Batch Invariance jobs, where the specialized tiers exist.

**Related.** #57016 and #57092 are about batch invariance of the MoE experts, a different component.

**AI assistance.** Prepared with AI assistance (Claude Code). I reviewed every changed line and the test logs.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix] Keep compressed-tensors wNa16 linear layers batch invariant
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Follow-up to #60479. With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`, the compressed-tensors `pack-quantized` linear scheme (`CompressedTensorsWNA16`, W4A16 and W8A16) still runs the Marlin GEMM, whose tiling and K-split depend on the number of tokens, so logprobs change with the batch size. This PR applies the same fix as #60479 to that scheme: in batch-invariant mode skip the Marlin kernel selection and repacking, keep the checkpoint layout, unpack the weight in `apply_weights()` and call `matmul_batch_invariant`. Without the flag nothing changes.

## Claims

- On `main`, `tests/v1/determinism/test_batch_invariance.py` fails for `RedHatAI/Qwen3-8B-quantized.w4a16` (dense), `RedHatAI/Qwen3-30B-A3B-quantized.w4a16` (MoE; its dense layers use this scheme) and `RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-quantized.w8a16`. ## Details

**Root cause.** `CompressedTensorsWNA16.create_weights` always builds a Marlin `MPLinearKernel` (`choose_mp_linear_kernel`), and `apply_weights` runs it. Marlin's results depend on the number of rows, so batch-invariant mode is silently violated; the determinism suite fails for every pack-quantized checkpoint tried, on A10 and B300, while the needle test often passes (greedy outputs usually survive the logprob differences).

**Change** (`compressed_tensors_wNa16.py` only). With `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`: no Marlin kernel is created, `process_weights_after_loading` keeps `weight_packed` / `weight_scale` / `weight_zero_point` in the checkpoint layout, and `apply_weights` unpacks the weight with `compressed_tensors.compressors.pack_quantized.helpers.unpack_from_int32` (and the zero points for asymmetric checkpoints), dequantizes in the scales dtype and calls `matmul_batch_invariant`. The log line becomes `Using dequantize + batch-invariant matmul for CompressedTensorsWNA16`.

**Trade-offs and limitations.**
- The weight is unpacked on every forward in batch-invariant mode (same choice as #60479: keeping a dequantized copy would need the memory of the unquantized model). The cost is in the benchmark blocks above.
- Symmetric W4A16 and W8A16 checkpoints and an asymmetric W4A16 checkpoint were validated (blocks above).
- The MoE expert path of compressed-tensors (`CompressedTensorsWNA16MoEMethod`) is not touched: on the MoE model tested the experts run through the Triton WNA16 MoE backend and the violation disappears once the dense layers are fixed.

commits.pr_title: [KV Offload] Split replicated-layout pre-faulting across workers
commits.pr_body:
With the replicated layout, every worker maps the same bytes, yet every worker still pre-faults the whole region. At TP4, that is four passes over one shm file, all contending for the same pages.

Give each worker one contiguous, page-aligned share to pre-fault instead. The pages are shared, so the region still ends up fully populated.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main). GLM-5.3 only uses the replicated layout with #57652, so these runs have that PR applied:

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 162.8 to 46.7 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1184 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.

commits.pr_title: [Bugfix][Compile] Replace Transformers AOT caching with graph caching
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

Fix compilation caching for the Transformers backend by running Dynamo tracing on each startup while reusing PyTorch graph caches.

Decorated HF `forward` methods can fail model-AOT serialization. Disabling model AOT alone is insufficient: direct artifact lookup can reuse stale compiled code when decorator state changes between processes.

Following the review suggestion, HF opts out through `support_torch_compile(..., use_aot_compile=False)`. The option is passed explicitly through `init_backend` to the backend, compiler manager, and adaptors:

- Skip model AOT, mega artifacts, and direct artifact loading/saving, including existing cache-index lookup.
- Retain PyTorch graph caching and initialize persistent Inductor/Triton cache directories.
- Preserve native AOT caching, including native EAGLE3 drafts under an HF target.

This replaces the earlier `CompileCachePolicy`, owner ContextVar, and loader changes. The opt-out applies in `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`; cache-disable settings remain respected. HF does not attempt forced model-AOT loading when opted out.

Related to #50128, specifically compilation caching. Follows the graph-caching recommendation in #53295 and preserves the cache-relocation behavior from #52142. This addresses HF cache routing rather than the cache-key API migration in #39517 or empty-artifact validation in #56879.

## Test Plan

- Fresh-process regression for changed decorator closure state, warm graph-cache hits, and repeated forward calls, covering both Inductor adaptors.
- Native AOT save/load after an opt-out module runs under the same configuration.
- Functorch configuration restoration on normal/exceptional exit and hash calculation; bypass of existing direct-cache metadata and handles.
- Three HF models and a native control under two cache-persistence protocols; real TP=2 and full HF-target/native-EAGLE3 generation.
- Full Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K evaluation under the batch-invariant compilation configuration described below.

## Test Results

### Warm startup: 8.9%–10.5% less time with persistent caches

Before is main at `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`; After is the smaller implementation described above.

Single L20, TP=1, BF16. Each model/backend/version/protocol has **1 cold + 5 fresh-process warm runs**, alternating A/B order. Values are `LLM(...)` initialization **median [min, max] in seconds**, excluding imports.

For the primary protocol, both versions receive persistent Inductor/Triton cache-directory settings. Caches are isolated by model/backend/version, and each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. Worker paths are verified because vLLM may redirect Inductor to its own persistent subdirectory.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 20.344 [20.105, 20.953] | **18.204 [17.595, 18.343]** | **10.52%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 15.570 [15.160, 16.111] | **14.121 [13.734, 14.297]** | **9.31%** |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 27.830 [27.769, 28.155] | **25.355 [25.183, 25.572]** | **8.89%** |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.857 [11.723, 11.978] | 11.719 [11.659, 12.030] | Ranges overlap |

The HF results are consistent in magnitude with the earlier 8–10% observation. No native speedup, throughput improvement, or TTFT improvement is claimed.

<details>
<summary>Supplement: only VLLM_CACHE_ROOT persists</summary>

Inductor/Triton directory overrides are unset; each process has private HOME/TMPDIR/XDG directories. This measures the case where only the vLLM cache root persists, rather than ordinary same-user restarts.

| Model / backend | Before warm, s | After warm, s | Time reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 30.274 [30.041, 31.056] | **18.180 [17.794, 18.358]** | **39.95%** |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 25.188 [24.725, 25.983] | **14.109 [13.875, 14.304]** | **43.98%** |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 37.718 [37.262, 38.034] | **24.810 [24.631, 25.560]** | **34.22%** |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 11.909 [11.545, 12.693] | 11.958 [11.618, 12.532] | Ranges overlap |

The **34.2%–44.0%** reduction is specific to this protocol. Compared with explicit lower-level caches, HF Before is 9.62–9.93 s slower; After differs by 0.011–0.545 s. Worker paths and cache counters support a cache-persistence explanation, without establishing per-kernel attribution. Independently compiled caches and shared-host load also limit cross-protocol attribution.

Native median changes are −1.17% with explicit caches and +0.41% with root-only persistence. Ranges overlap in both protocols; no consistent native regression or speedup is established.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Cold timings and reproducibility</summary>

| Model / backend | Explicit Before / After, s | Root-only Before / After, s |
|---|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 46.855 / 44.519 | 47.267 / 45.283 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 37.518 / 35.636 | 37.459 / 36.782 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 56.375 / 54.423 | 56.104 / 52.939 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 51.503 / 51.999 | 52.575 / 51.835 |

- **96/96 starts completed; all 96 cache checks passed.** No samples were discarded. These are new measurements of the smaller implementation, not reused smoke timings.
- Baseline: `9f3d70e08157a95911f15809f2f1446424825ea7`.
- Measured patch SHA256: `5edec6ae4c933e25df921c1c1d045b2ff277c0d8c56ed473ac12f99a2b2bf4eb`.
- Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.13.0+cu129, Transformers 5.15.1, Triton 3.7.1. A/B use identical hashes for the five rebuilt dense-runtime extensions.
- BF16, FlashAttention, seed=0, max model length=512, max batched tokens=512, max sequences=8, memory utilization=0.8, CUDA graph sizes `[1,2,4,8]`, four CPU/compilation threads.
- Raw AOT/mega/standalone flags are enabled; cache-disable and force-load are disabled. No batch invariance or additional deterministic controls are enabled. All workers use `CompilationMode.VLLM_COMPILE`.
- Fixed physical L20 GPU 4, checked idle before every start. Runs were serial within the task; the host was not CPU-exclusive. A/B never share compiled artifacts; remote graph caches are disabled.
- Cold means an empty compilation cache. OS page caches were not cleared; model-file verification may warm them. Single cold observations and five warm samples do not establish statistical significance.
- Qwen3-0.6B revision: `c1899de289a04d12100db370d81485cdf75e47ca`. TinyLlama and Qwen3-14B snapshots are identified by per-file SHA256.

</details>

### Correctness and cache behavior

- **HF:** all After warm performance runs hit FX/AOTAutograd caches; model-AOT/direct-artifact save/load counts remain zero.
- **Native:** all cold runs save AOT; all five warm runs per version/protocol load it with zero model-AOT recompilations. Separate forced-load checks also pass.
- **TP=2:** Qwen3-0.6B HF completes cold/warm initialization and generation on both versions. Both After ranks record three FX and three AOTAutograd hits on warm start, with separate rank cache directories.
- **EAGLE3:** full generation with Qwen3-0.6B HF and `Nicolassuez/Qwen3-0.6B-eagle3` completes across cold/warm processes. The HF target uses graph caching; the native draft saves AOT on cold start and loads it on warm start.
- **Cache disable:** separate HF cold/warm checks retain compilation while recording zero FX/AOTAutograd cache hits and zero model-AOT/direct-artifact saves or loads.

Performance runs generate the same 32 prompts after initialization, using batch sizes 1/4/8, greedy decoding, and up to 64 tokens. **All 128 comparisons pass the existing repository helper without relaxed tolerances; 124/128 contain token-sequence differences.** Each comparison covers 32 prompts; this count is not a prompt failure rate or an accuracy measurement.

| Model / backend | Explicit: comparisons with token differences | Root-only: comparisons with token differences | Helper failures |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-0.6B / HF | 16/16 | 16/16 | 0 |
| TinyLlama-1.1B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-14B / HF | 16/16 | 15/16 | 0 |
| Qwen3-0.6B / native | 14/16 | 16/16 | 0 |

Each group includes ten within-version cold/warm comparisons and six corresponding A/B comparisons. The helper checks first-divergence tokens against the other output's top-5; it does not establish full-sequence or accuracy equivalence.

### Qwen3-0.6B GSM8K

All **1,319 questions**, 5-shot, greedy decoding, 256-token generation limit. Before cold, After cold, and After warm each score **519/1319 (39.35%)**, with **identical per-question answers and complete token sequences**. Each run has 3 invalid answers and generates 132,670 tokens. After warm records **29 FX graph hits and 29 AOTAutograd hits**.

This uses batch invariance with compilation enabled, max model length=4096, max batched tokens=2048, and max sequences=8. Batch invariance disables model AOT upstream; mega/standalone remain enabled. This evaluation does not establish quality equivalence under the default AOT-enabled configuration or for Qwen3-14B. Evaluation timings are excluded from the performance results.

<details>
<summary>Numerical diagnostics and coverage limits</summary>

Default runs contain token differences across versions and between cold/warm starts within a version, despite passing the repository helper. Separate smaller-implementation smoke comparisons also pass the helper, with these token-sequence differences among 32 prompts:

| Path | Before cold → Before warm | Before cold → After cold | After cold → After warm |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| HF | 4/32 | 6/32 | 3/32 |
| Native | 4/32 | 1/32 | 4/32 |
| HF TP=2 | 7/32 | 5/32 | 6/32 |
| EAGLE3 | 2/32 | 2/32 | 3/32 |

These smoke comparisons are separate from the 128 performance-run comparisons above. Cache-disabled HF runs also differ on 5/32 prompts, showing that cache hits are not necessary for output variation; this does not rule out all effects of the patch.

The largest common-prefix logprob difference in the performance matrix is **4.312496** for Qwen3-14B: an unselected token has logprobs −13.250004 and −17.5625, while both runs select the same token at that position. This is not evidence of an incorrect selected token, but the differences should not all be described as negligible rounding. Operator-level attribution has not been established.

The batch-invariant GSM8K result is separate evidence with its own configuration limits. Full Qwen3-14B quality evaluation has not been repeated for this implementation. Earlier implementation-specific numerical controls and quality results are not counted as current validation.

Testing covers the recorded dependency environment and L20 GPUs. Required dense-runtime components were rebuilt from pinned source, but this is not a full wheel/Rust build, every optional extension, or full upstream CI. ROCm execution and a separate real `model_impl=auto` → HF resolution check remain unverified. The independent TinyLlama breakable-CUDA-graph issue is outside this patch.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Regression commands and results</summary>

Relevant suites ran with fresh vLLM cache roots and the verified task environment:

```bash
.venv-verified/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/compile/test_config.py

.venv-verified/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/compile/test_decorator.py \
  tests/compile/test_aot_compile.py \
  tests/compile/test_compiler_interface.py
```

- **127 passed, 1 skipped:** configuration tests 89 passed; decorator/AOT/compiler-interface tests 38 passed, 1 skipped.
- Six targeted mutations were detected: index read, direct load, configuration restoration, second forward, disabled native AOT, and hash-configuration restoration.
- A subsequent test-only isolation fix mocks adaptor cache initialization in the old-index test. A focused rerun including an environment-state probe reports **5 passed**; both index-read/direct-load mutations remain detected. Product code was unchanged. These counts are not additive, and the full suite was not rerun after this test-only change.
- Twelve applicable Python hooks passed on the smaller implementation; ruff, formatting, mypy, and diff checks were rerun after the isolation fix. Full pre-commit was blocked by offline actionlint dependency installation; full CI is not claimed.
- Existing binary/unpacked artifact-relocation tests are retained. The ROCm adaptor call site was updated, but ROCm tests were not executed locally.

Performance harness: `performance_controller.py`, `run_models.py`, `model_probe.py`, `export_results.py`, and `final_audit.py`. Per-run commands, environments, source hashes, worker paths/counters, full outputs, and exit codes were retained alongside the 96-sample CSV.

</details>

Assisted by Astra.

commits.pr_title: [Perf][Attention][MiniMax-M3] Select CUTLASS MSA by EAGLE3 decode shape
commits.pr_body:
## Overview

Select the MiniMax-M3 CUTLASS MSA decode path using measured SM103 EAGLE3
crossover points instead of a fixed batch-16 gate. The current patch is
model-local and keeps the original floor for unmeasured shapes and
architectures.

No other open PR changes this decode dispatch gate; #60684 changes prefill
query quantization and does not overlap this work.

## Claims in the current patch

- On SM103 with decode query lengths 1–8 and measured rank-local 64/4, 32/2,
  or 16/1 query/KV heads, use CUTLASS once
  `batch_size * decode_query_len * num_q_heads >= 1024`.
- Keep the existing batch-16 floor for query lengths 9–32, SM100, and unknown
  head geometries.
- Preserve all existing kernel constraints: explicit CUTLASS selection, FP8
  E4M3 KV cache, supported head geometry, page size 128, top-k 16, supported
  query length, and the planner row bound.
- Allow deployments to override the automatic crossover with the model-local
  `VLLM_MINIMAX_M3_MSA_CUTLASS_MIN_BATCH`; unset uses the automatic policy,
  and setting the integer to 16 restores the original floor.

## Validation

Full `pr-checklist` audit: [read the condensed report](https://gist.github.com/anish-shanbhag/e87258c8b3d501ac34195d91335ff1cb).

### Current PR refresh (2026-10-08)

- Added the review update as a fast-forward commit; no existing commits were
  rewritten.
- Removed the global `envs.py` registration and `tests/test_envs.py` changes.
  The final PR changes only the MiniMax MSA implementation and its existing
  kernel test.
- `pre-commit run --files tests/kernels/attention/test_minimax_m3_msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/msa_cutlass_sparse_decode.py vllm/models/minimax_m3/nvidia/sparse_attention_msa.py`:
  passed, including Ruff, formatting, mypy, test tethering, SPDX, and
  forbidden-import checks.
- CPU-safe direct checks: seven dispatch cases and two model-local override
  cases passed. `git diff --check` also passed.
- The local host does not have the PyTorch/CUDA test runtime, so the existing
  GB300 correctness and benchmark results below remain the GPU validation.

### Original query-length-4 GB300 evidence

The isolated benchmark used one NVIDIA GB300, EAGLE3 query length 4, FP8 E4M3
KV cache, 16 selected pages per token/KV head, CUDA graph replay, 30 warmups,
300 iterations, and five trials. It covered request batches 1/2/4/8/16, 8K
and 200K cached contexts, TP1/TP2/TP4, and concurrent DEP2/DEP4 ranks.

| Local heads | Batch 4 | Batch 8 | Batch 16 | First measured win | Query-head rows at win |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64/4 | 1.069x | 1.545x | 1.875x | 4 | 1,024 |
| 32/2 | 0.800x | 1.100x | 1.642x | 8 | 1,024 |
| 16/1 | 0.600x | 0.800x | 1.099x | 16 | 1,024 |

These conservative ratios charge CUTLASS for standalone BF16-to-FP8 query
quantization. All 130 rank-level CUTLASS-versus-Triton comparisons passed at
`atol=0.02`, `rtol=0.02`; maximum absolute error was `0.00006104`. The
focused GB300 kernel suite reported `41 passed` in 237.40 seconds, and the
focused environment suite reported `9 passed`.

### Query-length 1–8 follow-up (2026-10-08)

A second GB300 microbenchmark swept decode query lengths 1–8, TP1/TP2/TP4,
request batches 1/2/3/4/6/8/12/16/24/32/48/64, and cached contexts 8,192 and
200,064. It used interleaved CUDA-graph replay with the same 30 warmups, 300
iterations, and five trials. Query lengths 1/2/4/8 fit the rule; 3/5/6/7 were
held out. All 1,344 rank-level comparisons passed correctness at
`atol=rtol=0.02`; maximum absolute error was `0.00430298`.

The safe direct-kernel crossover is the first measured batch for which every
larger measured batch wins at both context lengths:

| Decode query length | TP1 / 64 Q heads | TP2 / 32 Q heads | TP4 / 16 Q heads |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 12 | 24 | 48 |
| 2 | 6 | 12 | 24 |
| 3 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| 4 | 3 | 6 | 12 |
| 5 | 2 | 4 | 8 |
| 6 | 2 | 4 | 6 |
| 7 | 2 | 3 | 6 |
| 8 | 2 | 3 | 6 |

The follow-up image (vLLM 0.25.0) first won at 768 query-head rows for query
length 4. The newer vLLM 0.28.1rc1 benchmark used only power-of-two batches,
so its first measured win at 1,024 rows did not test 768. At the shared 512-
and 1,024-row points, the two datasets agree to rounding (approximately
0.889x/0.800x and 1.222x/1.099x for direct/conservative speedup). This is not
evidence of a version shift, but the matching-version evidence does not resolve
the intermediate boundary. The merge-safe rule is therefore the conservative,
directly measured newer-image boundary:

```python
query_head_rows = batch_size * decode_query_len * num_q_heads
if 1 <= decode_query_len <= 8 and measured_head_geometry:
    automatic_min_batch = ceil_div(1024, decode_query_len * num_q_heads)
else:
    automatic_min_batch = 16
use_cutlass = batch_size >= automatic_min_batch
```

The 1,024-row rule produced zero false-positive CUTLASS regressions across all
576 new aggregated cases. It left 61 direct-kernel wins unselected on the
older image, an intentional conservative trade-off. This supports replacing
the `decode_query_len == 4` special case and three head-geometry entries with a
single query-head-row threshold, while retaining every existing capability,
dtype, head, page-size, top-k, maximum-query-length, and maximum-row guard.
Query lengths 9–32 retain the existing batch-16 floor rather than extrapolating
beyond the measured sweep. Unknown head geometries also retain 16.

The selected region has clear margin: among all 318 selected cases, the minimum
direct-kernel speedup was 1.221x and the minimum quantization-inclusive speedup
was 1.098x. The 24 cases at exactly 1,024 rows measured 1.221–1.223x direct and
1.098–1.101x with standalone quantization. Median per-case trial CV at the
boundary was 0.020% for Triton and 0.019% for the conservative CUTLASS path;
the maximum CVs were 0.199% and 0.063%, respectively.

The current commit implements the conservative 1,024 query-head-row rule for
query lengths 1–8. The 768-row rule remains a later candidate, but it should be
adopted only after measuring that intermediate point on the same vLLM build
used by the PR.

Complete tables, all trial JSON/CSV artifacts, methodology, and runnable
benchmark/analysis scripts are in the [benchmark Gist](https://gist.github.com/anish-shanbhag/3ce54e7314995b38b22612ab0100b260).

Matched MiniMax-M3-NVFP4 disaggregated EAGLE3 runs of the original fixed-16
policy versus an earlier blanket batch-4 experiment showed approximately
+3–5% p90 per-user output-token rate and +1–2.5% total TPS/GPU. That experiment
supports the opportunity but does not isolate the final dispatch policy; the
microbenchmarks above provide the shape-specific evidence.

## Details

### Root cause and implementation

The existing metadata builder used a fixed `batch_size >= 16` dispatch gate,
so common EAGLE3 verification steps fell back to Triton even when CUTLASS was
faster. A blanket lower floor is unsafe because tensor parallelism changes
rank-local query/KV head geometry and therefore the crossover. The current
model-local helper selects a conservative floor from query length, device
capability, and head geometry. The metadata builder resolves the optional
environment override once at initialization and passes it to the existing
dispatch predicate.

### Design fit and trade-offs

The implementation stays within MiniMax-M3's NVIDIA sparse-attention path and
does not change shared scheduler, model-runner, or KV-cache interfaces. The
automatic speedup is deliberately limited to the measured SM103 EAGLE3
query-length and head-geometry region; all other shapes keep the prior
batch-16 behavior.

## Checklist

- [x] Change is model-local and does not add complexity to shared core components.
- [x] Dispatch boundaries have targeted regression coverage; the integer
  override remains a model-local rollback.
- [x] Existing CUDA correctness and benchmark evidence exercises the changed path.
- [x] Query lengths 1–8 now have a genuine CUTLASS-versus-Triton microbenchmark.
- [x] Current lint, typing, test-tethering, and CPU-safe checks pass after rebasing.
- [x] Performance scope, fallback behavior, version calibration, and end-to-end limitations are explicit.
- [x] Commits are signed off and include AI-assistance attribution.

## AI assistance disclosure

This change, benchmark support, rebase, and PR refresh used OpenAI Codex. The
human submitter remains responsible for reviewing every changed line,
reproducing GPU validation as needed, and defending the implementation and
evidence end to end.

commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

Expose JSON response and SSE event schemas for chat and legacy completions in `/openapi.json`, using existing Pydantic models and OpenAPI 3.2. Related to #25272; broader client-generator issues are out of scope.

## Claims

- Both endpoints expose distinct unary JSON and SSE contracts with resolvable model references.
- SSE `itemSchema` describes an event envelope whose `data` is a JSON chunk, JSON error, or `[DONE]`. Keep-alive comments are not data events.
- Inference and stream generation are unchanged. Early disconnects now return an explicit empty `Response()` from the shared cancellation wrapper instead of `None`, avoiding response-model validation errors without making successful response schemas nullable.
- Bundled Swagger UI is updated to v5.33.1 so offline docs can load OpenAPI 3.2 documents. Rendering the SSE item schema remains an upstream limitation (see Details).

## Validation

Linux CPU checks were run by Codex at the author's request. The implementation and assertions in `b04e80127b` passed the checks below; the subsequent changes before committing only clarified test docstrings. The author confirmed validation and approved publishing this revision.

Before/after JSON captured through `GET /openapi.json` using the production routers and an in-process ASGI client, without an inference engine. These excerpts select HTTP 200 response content for the two endpoints, not the entire document. On a running server, reproduce this projection with:

```bash
curl -fsS http://localhost:8000/openapi.json | jq '
  .paths
  | with_entries(select(.key == "/v1/chat/completions" or .key == "/v1/completions"))
  | map_values(.post.responses["200"].content)'
```

Before (`4cf1307e72cb`):

```json
{
  "/v1/chat/completions": {
    "application/json": {"schema": {}},
    "text/event-stream": {}
  },
  "/v1/completions": {
    "application/json": {"schema": {}},
    "text/event-stream": {}
  }
}
```

After (`b04e80127b`; the document declares `"openapi": "3.2.0"`):

```json
{
  "/v1/chat/completions": {
    "application/json": {
      "schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ChatCompletionResponse"}
    },
    "text/event-stream": {
      "itemSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["data"],
        "properties": {
          "data": {
            "type": "string",
            "anyOf": [
              {"const": "[DONE]"},
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ChatCompletionStreamResponse"}
              },
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"}
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  },
  "/v1/completions": {
    "application/json": {
      "schema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/CompletionResponse"}
    },
    "text/event-stream": {
      "itemSchema": {
        "type": "object",
        "required": ["data"],
        "properties": {
          "data": {
            "type": "string",
            "anyOf": [
              {"const": "[DONE]"},
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/CompletionStreamResponse"}
              },
              {
                "contentMediaType": "application/json",
                "contentSchema": {"$ref": "#/components/schemas/ErrorResponse"}
              }
            ]
          }
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

The references resolve to generated model schemas in the same document's `components.schemas`; those definitions are omitted here. Direct payload tests check the selected models and reject malformed `choices`. Separate Schemathesis tests exercise real ASGI routes with synthetic serving-handler streams: chunks, errors, `[DONE]`, and keep-alive comments pass; malformed choices and non-JSON data fail.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/entrypoints/openai/test_openai_schema.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_api_utils.py \
  tests/entrypoints/serve/utils/test_sse_keep_alive.py \
  -k 'not test_openapi_stateless' -q
```

- **40 passed, 1 deselected**, with Schemathesis 4.21.6 and FastAPI 0.136.3; also **40 passed, 1 deselected** with the minimum FastAPI 0.133.0.
- Cancellation regression: restoring the old wrapper reproduces `ResponseValidationError` on disconnect; the updated wrapper passes both disconnect and normal-completion cases.
- Changed-file pre-commit hooks and the additional mypy 3.12 check passed before the final docstring clarification.
- Browser checks loaded `/docs`, `/openapi.json`, and Swagger assets in online/offline modes. The OpenAPI 3.2 document loads; SSE `itemSchema` is not displayed correctly (upstream issue below).
- Existing Buildkite coverage includes the test files. The model-backed `test_openapi_stateless`, inference evaluation, and benchmarks were **not run**; the focused tests do not establish a full model-backed suite pass.

## Details

Register unary/chunk models with FastAPI; `openapi_extra` restores the unary JSON ref because the additional response model otherwise replaces it. Request structure is unchanged, but FastAPI renames `FunctionCall` to `FunctionCall-Input`; name-dependent consumers may notice.

Set the production app's OpenAPI version to 3.2.0, which defines `itemSchema`. This is a document-version change; no FastAPI dependency bump is needed. The cancellation fix is in the shared decorator and therefore applies to its other callers too; it does not change mid-stream disconnect handling by `StreamingResponse`.

**Swagger UI limitation:** v5.33.1 can load the OpenAPI 3.2 document but does not yet render `itemSchema` for sequential media types properly: [swagger-api/swagger-ui#11065](https://github.com/swagger-api/swagger-ui/issues/11065). The SSE contract is present in `/openapi.json` and exercised by Schemathesis, even though Swagger's response-schema display is incomplete. The bundled upstream assets and license are retained verbatim.

commits.pr_title: [Model][MoE] Load MegaMoE experts directly into the DeepGEMM layout
commits.pr_body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

DeepSeek-V4 MegaMoE (also used by Kimi-K3) loads the routed experts into loader-side parameters, then `finalize_weights` asks the `DeepGemmMegaMoEBackend` (#58053) to transform them into DeepGEMM's layout and drops the loaded parameters, so any later `load_weights` has nowhere to write. The fused shared expert is built the same way, from a shared MLP whose weights the fusion then takes over.

This PR moves the layout into load time. The backend is selected when the experts are constructed, registers the kernel-layout tensors as the parameters (`create_weights`), and writes each checkpoint shard straight into them (`load_weight`). Whether the shared expert is fused is also decided at construction. Loading, reloading and updating weights then write into the tensors the kernel reads, and there is no MegaMoE post-load step left: `finalize_weights`, `finalize_mega_moe_weights` and the post-load hooks that only called them are removed (DeepSeek-V4 keeps its mHC hook).

## Claims

- `reload_weights` works with MegaMoE. DeepSeek-V4-Flash GSM8K after a reload: `main` 0.948 → 0.008, this PR 0.951 → 0.948.
- DeepSeek-V4.1 (MXFP8 shared expert) keeps its fused shared expert across a reload: `main` 0.898 → 0.010, this PR 0.904 → 0.901.
- An identity reload changes no parameter and moves no storage (0 of 1588 per-rank checksums, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP2).
- The shared expert has no second copy: its four kernel tensors are the parameters (DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP2: 76.6 GiB, same as `main`).
- Kimi-K3 drops its `finalize_weights` override and the `_mega_l*` buffers.

## Validation

GB200, real weights, `vllm serve`, `--moe-backend deep_gemm_mega_moe`, EP. GSM8K: 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy.

| model, parallelism | `main`: GSM8K → `reload_weights` → GSM8K | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP2, MTP k=2 | 0.948 → **0.008** | 0.951 → 0.948 |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP4 | 0.898 → **0.010** | 0.904 → 0.901 |
| Kimi-K3 (1.5T MXFP4), 4 nodes, TP4 × DP4, EP16 | 0.944 → 0.950, 137.52 GiB | 0.949 → 0.937 and 0.945 → 0.954 (two runs), 137.52 GiB |

The `main` column was measured before #58053; #58053 moved the transform into the backend but kept the post-load transform that drops the loaded parameters. On `main`, Kimi-K3 survives this reload only because the checkpoint is the same: its `finalize_weights` returns early once transformed experts exist, so reloaded expert weights never reach the kernels.

Neither DeepSeek run logs the shared-expert fusion fallback warning, so both keep the fused shared expert.

`tests/models/test_deepseek_v4_mega_moe.py` (68 passed on GB200):
- Shuffled, per-shard routed loads (with EPLB replicas) are compared against DeepGEMM's batched transform, including the real DeepGEMM CUDA transform.
- A second routed load updates the kernel tensors in place.
- Shared-expert shards (gate, up, down; weights and 1x32 scales, both `.w2.` and `.down_proj.` names) land where DeepGEMM's transform puts them; reloading one shard overwrites in place and leaves the other half alone; the returned names are the registered parameters (for `enable_weights_track`).
- The fusion decision at construction: fused for DeepSeek-V4-Flash (e8m0 128x128) and V4.1 (uint8 1x32) scales; not fused for an older DeepGEMM, BF16 shared experts, non-UE8M0 scales or scales that do not tile to 1x32.

`tests/models/kimi_k3/test_weight_loading.py` is removed: it only checked that the removed Kimi-K3 finalize ran once.

`pre-commit` passes.

Setup: the vLLM image `nightly-dev-arm64-cu130-ac9126e58aa7` plus this change, overlaid file by file with SHA-256 gates.

Reviews: Codex (gpt-6-astra), Kimi K3 and Claude Fable 5.1 audited this change. The two Codex should-fix findings (backend chosen for GPU 0 when the model is built on `meta` under `ipc_cache`; fused shared parameters reported under checkpoint names to weight tracking) are fixed and re-verified by Codex.

## Details

**Backend interface.** #58053's `transform_weights` / `transform_shared_expert_weights` / `supports_shared_experts(deep_gemm)` become:
- `create_weights(layer, ...)`: register the routed (and fused shared) parameters in the kernel layout, indexed by local expert on dim 0 (EPLB moves experts along it);
- `load_weight(dst, src, shard_id, is_scale)`: write one checkpoint shard into one expert slice or a shared parameter;
- `supports_shared_experts(shared_experts)`: decide fusion at construction.

A post-load transform cannot coexist with in-place weight updates, because it replaces the storage the loaders write into. A backend with a different layout (e.g. an SM90 plugin) expresses it in `create_weights` and `load_weight`. Out-of-tree backends written against #58053 need this migration.

**SM100 layout.** DeepGEMM's `transform_weights_for_mega_moe` interleaves gate/up rows in groups of 8 and permutes scale rows for UTCCP; the L2 weight is unchanged. Each row of each shard lands at a fixed position, so `load_weight` copies a shard into a strided view of its final location:
- L1 gate row `r` → `(r // 8) * 16 + r % 8`, up row `r` → `(r // 8) * 16 + 8 + r % 8`.
- Scales are the UE8M0 bytes expanded to one per 1x32 block, packed four along K per int32, stored MN-major, with the UTCCP row map `128b + 32j + i → 128b + 4i + j`.

Routed FP4 parameters are int8 (the kernel's dtype) instead of uint8; loads reinterpret the bytes.

**Shared expert.** Fusion requires FP8 shared weights with UE8M0 scales that tile to 1x32 (checked on the shared MLP's parameters, which its quant method creates at init) and a DeepGEMM with the shared-expert API. Otherwise it warns once and keeps the separate shared MLP, as on `main`, but at construction instead of after loading, so the layout never changes after load. When fused, `DeepseekV4MoE.shared_experts` is `None` and `load_weights` routes `shared_experts.*` tensors to the experts' four kernel-layout parameters.

**Backend selection.** The backend is selected for the device the model is built on, or for the worker's current GPU when that is `meta` (`--load-format ipc_cache`).

**Scope.** EPLB with a reload after a rebalance is broken on `main` and is not addressed. XPU keeps its own implementation.

**Not a duplicate.** #59003 (draft, stacked on #53509) also targets MegaMoE reload, but by staging new checkpoint sources and re-packing into buffers through a reload lifecycle. This PR removes the packed copy: the parameters are the kernel tensors, so there is nothing to stage or rebuild.

**AI assistance.** Written with Claude Code. The submitter reviewed every changed line and ran the tests and GPU checks above.

---
