commits.pr_title: [Attention] Fetch MLA prefill workspace at use instead of init
commits.pr_body:
## Purpose

The TRTLLM-ragged and FlashInfer MLA prefill backends keep a view of the shared workspace from `__init__`. When a later user, such as the sparse indexer's profile, grows the workspace, that view keeps the old buffer alive as an orphan. On GLM-5.3 on B200 that's 394 MB of GPU memory nobody uses.

Both backends now reserve their size at init without keeping a view, and fetch it in `prepare_metadata`, once per step. FlashInfer rebuilds its wrappers if the workspace has moved. The builder runs outside the DBO micro-batch threads, so both still use the micro-batch 0 slot, as on main.

Sharing the workspace is safe: TRTLLM ragged runs with multi-CTA KV off and uses it only for per-launch softmax stats, and FlashInfer cutlass prefill never touches it (it has its own 32 MB buffer).

## Test Result

Memory: 1×B200, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 cut to 4 layers with dummy weights, fp8 KV, `--max-model-len 1048576`, TRTLLM-ragged prefill:

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| Available KV cache | 138.64 GiB | 139.02 GiB |
| GPU KV blocks | 861,476 | 863,866 |
| Orphaned 0.38 GiB block from `trtllm_ragged.py` `__init__` | present | gone |

- Greedy token ids and logprobs are bit-identical to main, with chunked-context prefill, on GLM-5.3 (TRTLLM-ragged) and DeepSeek-V2-Lite (FlashInfer prefill forced). FlashInfer wrappers are built once per backend instance, as on main.
- GSM8K, GLM-5.3-NVFP4 TP4: main 0.906, this PR 0.908.
- `tests/v1/attention/`: `test_mla_prefill_selector`, `test_mla_prefill_registry`, `test_mla_prefill_quant_output`, `test_mla_noncausal`, `test_sparse_mla_backends`, `test_dspark_noncausal_sparse_mla` and `test_mla_backends` all pass on B200.

- New CPU test `test_prefill_backend_does_not_pin_grown_workspace` (both backends) fails on main and passes here.
- Results above re-checked at 82731e58f4 (fetch in `prepare_metadata`): same memory, outputs bit-identical, `test_mla_backends.py` 1793 passed. DBO not run (needs a DeepEP / NIXL-EP all2all build); the workspace slot it uses matches main.

<details><summary>Commands</summary>

Main is d80ddaac73; this PR is 82731e58f4.

```bash
VLLM_DEBUG_WORKSPACE=1 vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 --load-format dummy --hf-overrides '{"num_hidden_layers": 4}' \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 64 --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-seqs 16
vllm serve RedHatAI/GLM-5.3-NVFP4 -tp 4 --max-model-len 8192 --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --enforce-eager --block-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype fp8
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 256 --max-concurrency 32 --seed 42
```

commits.pr_title: [ROCm][Perf] W4A16: speed up skinny GEMM decode, including speculative batches
commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Tunes the W4A16 skinny GEMM decode path on gfx115x, and stops routing deep-K decode shapes away from it.

The kernel compiles for gfx11 and gfx12, and everything here was measured on gfx1151, so **every commit gates itself to gfx115x** -- the tuning and the routing alike. Off gfx115x the kernel runs exactly as it does today: the K * N bound stays at 1.2x LDS, the chunked path never launches, every tuple takes the checked K loop, the zero point keeps its own pass over the unpacked values, and the dispatch keeps its current tuples. The Python side gets an `on_gfx115x()` platform helper so the layer routes to match the C++ host check.

Eight commits, each measured against its parent on gfx1151 / ROCm 10.2, median of 3 passes:

| commit | what | effect |
|---|---|---|
| test coverage | asymmetric path and batch 4/5 at the op level | — |
| K loop | instantiate the whole-block loop without the bound check | mean **+18.9%**, 44 of 46 cells |
| zero point | fold it into the fp16 dequant constants | up to **+28.8%** at batch 1, asymmetric |
| group stride | scale and zero-point rows get their own row stride, HIP and Triton | — |
| LDS bound | stop rejecting K * N past the LDS budget | **+67% / +90%** on the shape that crosses it |
| chunked K | walk K in LDS-sized chunks so every activation row stays in LDS | **+30.5% / +51.7%** at batch 4, deep K |
| dispatch rules | avoid trimming wave slots, widen loads for deep-K batch 1 | **+9.4% to +16.3%** |
| LDS band | store the chunked activation band piece-major, conflict-free | **+1.9%** mean on chunked shapes |

## Results

The GEMM shapes a `cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` decode step issues, at group size 32 and asymmetric, driven through `rdna_hybrid_w4a16_apply` so the HIP/Triton routing is the production one. Percentages are bytes moved over elapsed time against 230 GB/s of practical board bandwidth. Median of 3 passes against `main`.

| Workload | Shape (M×K) | Kernel | main | this branch | Gain |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Decode, N=1 | 43008×5376 | sml | 634.8 µs — 92% | 499.2 µs — 116% ⁽¹⁾ | **−21.4%** |
| Decode, N=1 | 5376×21504 | sml | 360.7 µs — 81% | 325.5 µs — 89% | −9.8% |
| Decode, N=1 | 16384×5376 | sml | 266.7 µs — 83% | 242.1 µs — 92% | −9.2% |
| Decode, N=1 | 5376×8192 | sml | 144.0 µs — 77% | 129.9 µs — 85% | −9.8% |
| Decode, N=1 | 5376×16384 | sml | 296.0 µs — 75% | 263.8 µs — 84% | **−10.9%** |
| Decode, N=1 | 20480×5376 | sml | 334.8 µs — 83% | 303.5 µs — 91% | −9.3% |
| Spec decode, N=2 | 5376×21504 | Triton → chunked | 474.9 µs — 61% | 313.8 µs — 93% | **−33.9%** |
| Spec decode, N=2 | 5376×16384 | sml | 295.3 µs — 75% | 264.1 µs — 84% | **−10.6%** |
| Spec decode, N=3 | 5376×21504 | Triton → chunked | 498.7 µs — 58% | 315.3 µs — 92% | **−36.8%** |
| Spec decode, N=3 | 5376×16384 | Triton → chunked | 728.0 µs — 30% | 259.5 µs — 86% | **−64.4%** |
| Spec decode, N=4 | 5376×21504 | Triton → chunked | 499.2 µs — 58% | 316.0 µs — 92% | **−36.7%** |
| Spec decode, N=4 | 5376×16384 | Triton → chunked | 743.4 µs — 30% | 256.1 µs — 87% | **−65.6%** |

The speculative-decode rows carry the routing change: today any shape with K * batch past the LDS budget goes to the Triton prefill kernel, which at N=3 and K=16384 runs at 30% of bandwidth. Run-to-run spread is under 4% on every cell except that one, where it is 7.6%; the effect there is an order larger.

⁽¹⁾ Above 100% because the denominator charges scales and zero points to DRAM; for this shape that working set is 18 MB and fits the 32 MB MALL. The weight stream alone is 115.6 MB in 499.2 µs, 232 GB/s, which is the board's practical ceiling.

## Accuracy

GSM8K, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42, on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ` with `max_num_seqs=4`:

| | main | this branch |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| strict-match | 0.8582259287338894 | 0.8582259287338894 |
| flexible-extract | 0.8612585291887794 | 0.8612585291887794 |

Identical to the last digit, so every one of the 1319 answers matches. `max_num_seqs=4` is load-bearing: Qwen3-8B has K = 4096 and K = 12288, so at batch 1 nothing crosses the LDS budget and none of the routing changes engage. At batch 4 the down projection gives K * N = 49152, which goes to Triton today and stays on the chunked path here -- the eval runs straight through the largest behavioural change in the series and produces the same output.

The deep-K tuple is not covered by this eval, and cannot be by any Qwen3-8B: it needs K divisible by 8192, and this model has neither. It is covered at the op level instead, by test cases at K = 8192 and K = 16384.

## End to end

`cyankiwi/gemma-4-31B-it-AWQ-4bit` served on gfx1151, 328 in / 256 out, 10 prompts each carrying one 640×480 image, batch 1:

| | main | this branch | |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **TPOT** | 120.7 ms | **107.4 ms** | **−11.0%** |
| **Decode throughput** | 7.65 tok/s | **8.49 tok/s** | **+11.0%** |
| End-to-end latency | 33.47 s | 30.15 s | −9.9% |
| TTFT | 2691 ms | 2762 ms | +2.6% |

TTFT is prefill. Routing there is unchanged, and the Triton kernel's arithmetic is too, but its scale and zero-point addressing now goes through a row stride instead of assuming K / group_size; for a contiguous tensor that stride is the same value and the generated code is unchanged.

This understates the series: at batch 1 on an AWQ checkpoint the chunked path, the wave-packing rule and the deep-K tuple all stay inactive, so the number above comes from the first four commits alone. The last three target speculative decoding and deep-K projections, which this configuration does not exercise.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/kernels/quantization/test_rdna_hybrid_w4a16.py` on gfx1151: 197 passed. Cases added for the deep-K instantiations, for each batch that reaches the chunked path, for a K that crosses a chunk boundary with a ragged tail, and for group size 32 where one unrolled step spans exactly one scale group.
- [x] `pre-commit run` clean on every touched file, clang-format included.
- [x] End to end served on gfx1151 with an image workload, `main` against this branch.
- [x] GSM8K 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy, seed 42 on `Qwen/Qwen3-8B-AWQ`: identical to the last digit.

## AI assistance

AI assistance was used for this change, as required by `AGENTS.md`. Not a duplicate: the only other open PR touching `csrc/rocm/skinny_gemms_int4.cu` is #57015, which adds an alignment hint to the activation load in the compute body and changes neither the K loop, the dequant path nor the dispatch.

commits.pr_body:
## Summary

Add metadata-driven ModelOpt block quantization support through b12x for IQ2_XS, IQ2_XXS, and Q8_0 checkpoints on SM120/SM121 GPUs, including packed linear/MoE weights, Q8_0 embeddings/vectors, and NVFP4 W4A16 linear execution.

```text
config.json per-layer quantization metadata
  -> ModelOpt block codec selection
  -> packed weight loading and tensor-parallel slicing
  -> b12x kernel preparation before CUDA graph capture
  -> BF16-activation execution
```

This is a republication of Luke Alonso's #59486 from `askliar/vllm`, following our discussion about moving the submission so Luke can review the integration. The three source commits are squashed into one commit authored and committed by Andrii Skliar. Includes focused pre-commit fixes for loader type annotations and accelerator test APIs. This PR is intended to replace #59486; it does not introduce an independent implementation. #59486 remains open at submission time.

AI assistance was used in the original implementation/testing and to prepare this republication and description.

## Evidence

- Pre-commit repair: renamed the checkpoint quantization config local and typed the weight stream as an iterable; migrated synchronization and allocation queries in two GPU test files to `torch.accelerator`. CUDA API hook and Ruff check/format pass on all 14 changed Python files. Pinned mypy 1.20.2 passes for the loader and both test files with Python targets 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13. GPU tests were not rerun.
- Checks run during republication: `git diff --check a21a3f2ec76a02fada576b7e581a56307fb3e78f...HEAD` and `ruff check --no-cache` for all 14 changed Python files. Both passed.
- Source-author reported validation on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell with CUTLASS 4.7.1: focused GPU suite **13 passed, 67 deselected**; architecture compatibility **6 passed, 6 deselected**; serving **6/6 passed**, including an image request; full and piecewise CUDA graph capture succeeded.
- Source-author reported GSM8K smoke evaluation: **7/8 correct**, zero invalid outputs, eight questions, zero-shot, 1,024 output-token limit, concurrency two. Commit notes explicitly state that serving/evaluation used a separate RADIO compatibility commit; that commit is not included here.
- GPU, serving, and model evaluation tests were not rerun during republication. The source commit also records dynamic embedding GPU regression execution as pending; the available validation summaries do not establish whether that specific coverage subsequently ran.

Source test commands (require compatible b12x and GPU):

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/quantization/test_modelopt.py \
  -k 'block_quant or q8_vector' -q
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/kernels/moe/test_b12x.py \
  tests/model_executor/kernels/test_b12x_linear.py \
  -k 'block_quant or q8_embedding or nvfp4_w4a16_preserves' -q
```

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way

**Blast Radius:** quantization

Affects ModelOpt block-quantized loading and b12x execution, including routing/embedding paths and CUDA graph preparation. Pins the optional b12x dependency and Spark CI to 1.5.0. Runtime validation of this exact head remains necessary before merge.
